records.name: Pituitary gland
records.note: The release's only intracranial endocrine gland with geometry, and one of only three endocrine glands it carries at all.
records.position: A pea-sized oval gland suspended from the underside of the brain by the infundibulum, seated in the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone and roofed by the diaphragma sellae (S1).
records.parts: Two functionally distinct parts. The anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) is glandular epithelium derived from Rathke's pouch, an ectodermal outpouching of the roof of the pharynx; its regions are the pars distalis — the largest and most hormonally active — the pars intermedia and the pars tuberalis (S1). The posterior lobe (neurohypophysis) is neurosecretory tissue derived from the embryonic forebrain and is functionally an extension of the hypothalamus (S1). The release carries the gland as an undivided leaf in both tables: no lobe or part of it exists as a concept (probe-verified), so the parts are sourced text on this record.
records.products: Anterior lobe (S4, Table 17.3): growth hormone (GH), prolactin (PRL), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinising hormone (LH). Intermediate zone: melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) (S4). Posterior lobe: it synthesises nothing itself — it stores and releases antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and oxytocin, which are synthesised in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus (S1, S4).
records.relations: Anteriorly the sphenoid sinus — the route of trans-sphenoidal surgical access. Superiorly the diaphragma sellae and the optic chiasm: an expanding pituitary adenoma presses on the chiasm and produces bitemporal hemianopia. Laterally the cavernous sinuses. Posteriorly the posterior intercavernous sinus, the dorsum sellae, the basilar artery and the pons; inferiorly the sphenoid sinus again (S1).
records.vasculature: The anterior lobe is fed through the hypophyseal portal system: the superior hypophyseal artery, a branch of the internal carotid, supplies a primary capillary plexus in the median eminence; portal veins carry that blood to a secondary plexus in the anterior lobe, delivering hypothalamic releasing and inhibiting hormones at high concentration (S1). The posterior lobe is supplied by the superior hypophyseal, infundibular and inferior hypophyseal arteries; the gland drains by hypophyseal veins (S1).
records.control: The hypothalamus — the nervous module's record brain.hypothalamus, the floor of the diencephalon anterior and inferior to the thalamus — is both a neural and an endocrine structure (S4): it governs the anterior lobe through the portal blood supply (S1) and owns the posterior lobe's hormones outright, the lobe being its own axonal extension (S1, S4).

records.name: Thyroid gland
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/endo_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — the release contains no thyroid gland concept in either parts list; every 'thyroid' name it carries is the thyroid cartilage (skeletal module), the inferior thyroid arteries (cardiovascular module) or the sternothyroid and cricothyroid muscles (muscular module)

arterial_supply: the inferior thyroid arteries are cardiovascular inventory records (artery.left-inferior-thyroid-artery, artery.right-inferior-thyroid-artery), resolved by the checker; the superior thyroid artery has no cardiovascular record of its own because its parent, the external carotid artery, is one of the concepts Milestone 5 found absent from the release
records.note: Sourced-text record: the dataset carries the gland's arteries, its cartilage namesake and the muscles named for it, but not the gland.
records.position: In the anterior neck, spanning vertebral levels C5 to T1: two lobes joined across the midline by a central isthmus, the whole gland butterfly-shaped, its lobes wrapping the cricoid cartilage and the superior tracheal rings, enclosed in the pretracheal fascia of the visceral compartment of the neck (S2).
records.structure: The working unit is the thyroid follicle: spheres of follicular cells around a colloid store, and the follicles are the site of hormone production (S5). Between them sit the parafollicular cells (S5). Each lobe carries parathyroid glands embedded in it, primarily on its posterior surface (S5) — see the companion record gland.parathyroid-glands.
records.products: The follicles produce the metabolic hormones thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), for which iodine is an essential component; they raise the basal metabolic rate (S5). The parafollicular cells produce calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium (S5).
records.arterial_supply: The superior thyroid artery, the first branch of the external carotid artery, descends to the upper pole close to the external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. The inferior thyroid artery arises from the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian artery and approaches the gland close to the recurrent laryngeal nerve. In about 10% of people a thyroid ima artery arises from the brachiocephalic trunk (S2).
records.venous_drainage: A venous plexus on the gland drains by the superior, middle and inferior thyroid veins: the superior and middle veins end in the internal jugular vein, the inferior veins in the brachiocephalic vein (S2).
records.nerves_at_risk: The recurrent laryngeal nerve — a branch of the vagus (the nervous module's clinical record nerve.cn-10-vagus) — is the surgically load-bearing relation of this gland. It branches from the vagus in the chest, hooks around the right subclavian artery on the right and around the arch of the aorta on the left, ascends in the tracheoesophageal groove and passes underneath the thyroid gland to reach the larynx it innervates; it lies close to the inferior thyroid artery and is at risk in thyroid surgery (S2). The external branch of the superior laryngeal nerve runs close to the superior thyroid artery at the upper pole (S2).
records.lymphatic_drainage: Lymph drains to the paratracheal and deep cervical lymph nodes (S2). Neither group exists as a concept in the release — the lymphatic module's census carries no lymph node of any kind — so this drainage is sourced text only.
records.control: Secretion is not under direct nervous control — the sympathetic fibres the gland receives do not govern it (S2); it is pituitary-regulated: thyrotropin-releasing hormone drives thyroid-stimulating hormone, TSH drives T4 and T3 release, and the thyroid hormones feed back negatively on the axis (S2, S5).

records.name: Parathyroid glands
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/endo_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — 'parathyroid' scores zero hits in both parts lists and in all six release tables
arterial_supply: no value asserted — none of the sources consulted in this session states the parathyroid glands' arterial supply in citable form; the field stays null rather than unsourced
records.note: Sourced-text record; the glands' surgical weight is inverse to their size, and the dataset carries no trace of them.
records.position: Tiny, round glands usually embedded in the posterior surface of the thyroid gland (S6); most people have four, though occasionally more are found in the tissues of the neck or chest (S6). Each is separated from the thyroid tissue by its own thick connective-tissue capsule (S6).
records.products: Parathyroid hormone (PTH), produced and secreted by the glands' chief cells in response to low blood calcium (S6).
records.function: PTH defends blood calcium: it stimulates osteoclasts to release calcium from bone, inhibits osteoblasts, increases calcium reabsorption in the kidney tubules, and initiates the production of calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D (S6). Its antagonist is calcitonin, secreted by the thyroid's parafollicular cells (S6) — the pairing that makes the two glands one surgical field.
records.cells: The chief cells are the primary functional cells of the gland, producing and secreting PTH; the oxyphil cells' function is not clear (S6).
records.relations: The glands sit within the posterior surface of the thyroid lobes, inside the thyroid's surgical field and separated from its tissue only by their capsule (S6) — which is why they, and the recurrent laryngeal nerve beside them, are what thyroid surgery must not take with the gland (see gland.thyroid-gland, nerves_at_risk).

records.name: Adrenal glands
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for the adrenal cortex, the adrenal medulla or any cortical zone (probe-verified over all six release tables); the cortex and medulla fields are sourced text on the two whole-gland records
records.note: Owned by this module per the release's own filing (Milestone 12 finding): the glands are direct members of the endocrine system in PART-OF and instances of the adrenal class in IS-A; Milestone 12's urinary census pointed here and this record closes that pointer.
records.position: Paired glands seated over the medial aspect of the upper poles of the kidneys, in the posterior abdomen between the superomedial kidney and the diaphragm; retroperitoneal, with parietal peritoneum on their anterior surface only (S3). The right gland is pyramidal, the left semi-lunar (S3). The perinephric (renal, Gerota) fascia encloses each gland with its kidney and attaches to the diaphragmatic crura, but fibrous tissue separates gland from kidney within it (S3) — the anatomical basis on which the urinary module censused these glands as this module's cross-reference rather than its own.
records.cortex: The outer zone of the gland, derived from embryonic mesoderm, yellowish, secreting the cholesterol-derived corticosteroids and androgens (S3). Its three zones run superficial to deep in a fixed order: the zona glomerulosa secretes the mineralocorticoids (aldosterone); the zona fasciculata secretes the corticosteroids (cortisol) and a small amount of androgens; the zona reticularis secretes the androgens (dehydroepiandrosterone) and a small amount of corticosteroids (S3).
records.medulla: The central zone, dark brown, derived from ectodermal neural crest: its chromaffin cells secrete the catecholamines (adrenaline) and enkephalins, the hormonal arm of the flight-or-fight response (S3).
records.products: Cortex: mineralocorticoids — aldosterone (zona glomerulosa); corticosteroids — cortisol (zona fasciculata); androgens — dehydroepiandrosterone (zona reticularis) (S3). Medulla: catecholamines, principally adrenaline, with enkephalins (S3). Hormone names are asserted here only as the consulted source names them.
records.relations: Right gland: anteriorly the inferior vena cava and the right lobe of the liver, posteriorly the right crus of the diaphragm. Left gland: anteriorly the stomach, the pancreas and the spleen, posteriorly the left crus (S3). Arteries and nerves enter at numerous sites around each gland, while veins and lymphatics leave through a hilum (S3).
records.arterial_supply: Three tiers (S3): the superior adrenal arteries from the inferior phrenic arteries; the middle adrenal arteries directly from the abdominal aorta; the inferior adrenal arteries from the renal arteries. The cardiovascular module carries the middle and inferior tiers under the release's own naming as the middle and inferior suprarenal arteries (records artery.left-middle-suprarenal-artery, artery.right-middle-suprarenal-artery, artery.left-inferior-suprarenal-artery, artery.right-inferior-suprarenal-artery), resolved by the checker.
records.venous_drainage: Asymmetric, and surgically load-bearing for it: the right adrenal vein drains directly into the inferior vena cava, the left adrenal vein into the left renal vein (S3). The cardiovascular module carries both as the suprarenal veins (vein.right-suprarenal-vein, vein.left-suprarenal-vein).
records.innervation: From the coeliac plexus and the greater splanchnic nerves (S3); the medulla is driven directly by myelinated preganglionic fibres, mainly from T10 to L1 — the medulla is, in effect, a sympathetic ganglion that secretes into the blood (S3).
records.lymphatics: Lymph drains to the lumbar lymph nodes through two plexuses, one deep to the capsule and one within the medulla (S3). No lumbar node exists as a concept in the release (lymphatic module census).

records.name: Pineal gland
verify: geometry held by the nervous module: the release files the pineal body inside the nervous system tree, where it is the nervous inventory record brain.pineal-body (FMA62033, Milestone 9); this record carries the gland's endocrine account and does not duplicate the mesh link
records.note: Cross-module record: geometry in the nervous module (brain.pineal-body), function here — the release's filing split, kept, with each side pointing at the other.
records.position: A tiny endocrine gland of the diencephalon, lying inferior but somewhat posterior to the thalamus (S7). The release files the pineal body inside the nervous system tree — under the epithalamus — and the nervous module holds its geometry; this record is its endocrine account.
records.products: Melatonin, an amine hormone derived from serotonin, produced and secreted by the gland's pinealocytes (S7).
records.function: Melatonin secretion entrains the circadian rhythms — sleepiness and wakefulness, and with them appetite and body temperature (S7). The source is explicit that the gland's functions are not entirely understood (S7); nothing further is asserted here.
records.regulation: Secretion varies with environmental light: photons striking the retina signal the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the hypothalamus, which relays through the spinal cord to the pineal and inhibits melatonin production — levels fall and wakefulness follows; in darkness production rises and drowsiness follows (S7).

records.name: Pancreatic islets
verify: no BP3D 4.0 concept exists for this structure (probe-verified over all six release tables by tools/endo_map.py); the record is sourced text only and links no geometry — 'islet' and 'langerhans' score zero hits in both parts lists and in all six release tables
records.note: Sourced-text record on another module's organ: the endocrine pancreas exists in the clinical layer only, exactly as far as the consulted source describes it.
records.definition: Clusters of endocrine cells scattered through the pancreas — formerly called the islets of Langerhans — which secrete glucagon, insulin, somatostatin and pancreatic polypeptide into the blood (S8). The pancreas that hosts them is primarily an exocrine gland (S8).
records.cell_types: Four cell varieties, in the proportions the consulted source gives: alpha cells about 20% of the islet, beta cells about 75%, delta cells about 4%, and PP cells about 1% (S8).
records.products: Alpha cells secrete glucagon, which raises blood glucose and is released when glucose is low; beta cells secrete insulin, which reduces blood glucose; delta cells secrete somatostatin, which inhibits the release of both glucagon and insulin; PP cells secrete pancreatic polypeptide (S8).
records.host_organ: The host organ is the pancreas — a long, slender organ lying mostly posterior to the bottom half of the stomach (S8) — which is the digestive module's inventory record pancreas and clinical record organ.pancreas (Milestone 11); the islets are censused there as this module's cross-reference boundary in reverse. No islet, and no part of the endocrine pancreas, has a concept in the release.
